rendered: Cathode: the anode-free full cell uses pyrite (FeS2) as the cathode, chosen as a cheap, abundant material.[1] Preparation: pyrite natively contains no sodium, so it is presodiated before cell assembly, and the full cell is built from presodiated pyrite paired with carbon/Al current collectors, i.e. in a discharged state. During the first charge, sodium ions leave the pyrite and are reduced on the carbon/Al collector to form sodium metal in situ, so the cell does not contain sodium metal on assembly.[2][3][4] Cathode capacity assumed for the energy density: the energy density (quoted as ∼400 Wh/kg[5]) was calculated from the mass of the presodiated pyrite, assuming a stoichiometry of Na1.5FeS2[6] and an FeS2 capacity of 335[7] mAh/g, together with the carbon nucleation layer.
